newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Grand Met to go to 650p long-term.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Grand Met to go to 650p long-term.

text.p: DAY'S RANGE * SUPPORT * RESTNCE* MA-25 * MA-200
+ Grand Metropolitan shares face near-term resistance at 520p but once this has been overcome a move up to 650p is possible over the long-term, technical analysts said.

+ The shares have moved roughly in-line with the alcoholic beverages sector so far this year and a long-term relative chart of the share price divided by the All-Share index shows the stock's underperformance since 1982 may have been arrested.
Shares in food and drinks company Grand Metropolitan GMET. have the potential to go up to 650p over the long-term, technical analysts said.
From a low of 429p at the start of the year the stock has been in an upward channel formed by the stock price rallying, falling back then rallying again.
It last made a prominent spike up from 477p at the start of the month and now appears to be winding back a little so there may be difficulty pushing too far ahead of 500p near-term, analysts said.
By 1445 GMT, the shares were unchanged at 499p.
The alcoholic beverage sector has a similar profile to Grand Met's share price and being a component of that sector, Grand Met has been performing roughly in-line with it this year.

"Alcoholic beverages have started to rally this year having found long-term support -- from the 1987 relative low -- and this looks like the beginning of a long-term turnaround," said Louise Kliem, technical analyst at Merrill Lynch.

"Grand Metropolitan looks particularly attractive since there's a longer-term chart objective of 650p if resistance at 500p gives way," she added. "In the near-term, there's resistance not too far away at around 520p."

A long-term chart of the relative performance of Grand Met against the All Share index highlights how badly the stock has fallen back relative to the market since 1982 but this slide may have been halted and a slow revival about to begin.
"The stock's relative charts are now suggesting a long-term upturn verses the market," said Kliem.
